surfaces.name: TB1
surfaces.note: USED not measurable from python — TB1's rail is the BROWSER, not the disk. ⚠ ADVERTISED 1024 GB = 30 GB PERMANENT + 994 GB that EXPIRES in -1.9 days (2026-08-14). Durable capacity is 30 GB — the SMALLEST cloud surface we own (GDX=100, ODX=1024). NOT a vault. What happens to files above 30 GB at expiry is UNKNOWN — TeraBox publishes no ToS answer and SGH could not find one. Do not store anything here you cannot lose on 2026-08-14.

credit.note: ONE-TIME credit, expires 2026-10-13. It does NOT renew daily. Unspent credit is DESTROYED. To use it all you must burn $5.03/day; you are burning $0.2658/day, so you are on track to WASTE $276.08.
credit._warning: DO NOT SOUND AN ALARM WITH THESE NUMBERS. 'spent' is bts_vertex.py's own token arithmetic, NEVER reconciled against Google. 'projected_waste' is a projection of that estimate and was the source of the fabricated '$299 waste' on 2026-07-15. Worse: it is not established that the $300 pays for Agent Platform AT ALL — no Google page states it, so a 'waste' figure may be measuring a credit that was never spendable here. VERIFY IN Billing→Reports (group by SKU): 'Other savings' NEGATIVE with Subtotal $0.00 = the credit paid. NOT the Cloud Hub Optimization page — that shows GROSS cost with credits invisible. Billing data lags up to 24h.
credit._expires_source: COMPUTED (start+90d), NOT read from the console. Terms §1.3 says the earlier of '$300 spent' or '3 MONTHS' — and Google uses '3 months'/'90 days' interchangeably though they differ. Read Billing→Overview and fix CREDIT_EXPIRES in bts_vertex.py.

policy.name: FAST
policy.why: Turns SEARCH on. This is the expensive step, not the model: a grounded call is $0.029 — 67x a plain one — because search injects ~10k tokens AND bills $0.005 per search. Worth it only when the answer needs FRESH web/X knowledge.

internodes.note: free, and the fastest rail we have. NEVER ask a model for a DOI.
8 MB: write 18 ms (449 MB/s), read 12 ms (640 MB/s). LOCAL Drive cache — NOT the cloud round trip a remote node pays (that is bts_gdxbench.py).
READ ONLY for the nodes. 5 KB in 215 ms = 24 KB/s. Only COWORK can WRITE (R2 keys).
Gemini API, free tier. Reply: OK

Chrome bridge. MEASURED 2026-07-13 via DOM observer + a HUMAN-pressed send. TTFT 254 ms, round trip 2093 ms. TRIVIAL PROMPT ONLY. The old '30-90 s' was COWORK's driving overhead, not the wire — the wire beats both APIs.

PROVEN 2026-07-14: SGH AUTHORS FILES TO GDX ON COMMAND (CH4-REVIEW-SGH.md, 5,383 B, correct folder). 'SGH cannot write to GDX' was FALSE and cost a week of routing design. RULES: the write must be its OWN turn (a bare 'write X to Y' — NOT 'write your previous message verbatim', which yields a 79-byte stub); give the folder by ID (1aiMjVZfFtiBGNAlkTwAYiq1Pvuz2F6hA), never by name; and VERIFY BY LISTING THE FOLDER, never by filename and never by its 'DONE'. See SOP_NODE_WRITES.md.

NEW RAIL 2026-07-14 (Keith found it): drive.google.com/drive/ai = GEMINI WITH NATIVE DRIVE READ, over the DOM, FREE (promotional; limits/expiry unstated). VERIFIED: read a GDX file back byte-for-byte. It CANNOT create files (says so plainly) — but its 'Export to Docs' button lands a real Google Doc in Drive that Cowork reads via the Drive API. ⇒ THE LOOP CLOSES: SGH writes -> GEM reads/analyses -> Export to Docs -> Cowork reads. A verifiable artifact at every hop, $0, and COWORK'S CONTEXT IS NEVER THE TRANSPORT.
BOTH ARE GROK. Not a channel to optimise — a correlation to distrust. Never use one to check the other.

bus.note: Theoretical max speedup = fanout (4x). Efficiency = what the bus actually delivered. Well under 100% means the bus — not the nodes — is the limit.
